source: derived from the clause 4.1.3 field layout
note: Complete Space Packets: primary header plus data field. The error control field is not defined by CCSDS 133.0-B-2 — it is a mission or PUS-style extension carried inside the packet data field, wire-compatible because the standard leaves the data field content to the mission. Where a vector uses it, the note says what the CRC covers.

encode.name: tm-apid-100-unsegmented-seq-5
encode.note: version 000, type 0 (TM), secondary header flag 0, APID 0x064, sequence flags '11' (unsegmented), count 5, data field 4 octets so the length field is 4-1 = 3. Bytes: 00 64 c0 05 00 03 then de ad be ef.

encode.name: tc-apid-123-unsegmented
encode.note: A telecommand, so the type bit is set: byte 0 = 1<<4 | 0x123>>8 = 0x11, byte 1 = 0x23. One octet of data means a length field of 0. Bytes: 11 23 c0 00 00 00 then 42.

encode.name: idle-packet-apid-all-ones
encode.note: An idle packet carries APID 'all ones' (0x7ff) and fill data. Bytes 0-1 = 07 ff, two fill octets so the length field is 1. Bytes: 07 ff c0 00 00 01 then ff ff.

encode.name: tm-with-error-control
encode.note: The optional error control field is the last two octets of the data field, so it counts toward the length: 4 data octets plus 2 CRC octets gives a data field of 6 and a length field of 5. The CRC-16-CCITT covers the primary header and the data field before the CRC itself, that is 00 64 c0 00 00 05 a1 b2 c3 d4, giving 0x6956.

decode.name: tm-apid-100-inverse
decode.note: The inverse of tm-apid-100-unsegmented-seq-5. A decoder must recover the APID, the sequence count and the data field from these octets.

decode.name: idle-packet-inverse
decode.note: The inverse of idle-packet-apid-all-ones. A receiver identifies an idle packet by its APID and discards it, so the APID must come back exactly.

reject.name: length-field-longer-than-the-octets-present
reject.note: The length field says the data field is 0x0003+1 = 4 octets, but only two follow the header. A decoder must refuse rather than read past the buffer.

reject.name: apid-above-eleven-bit-field
reject.note: 2048 does not fit the 11-bit APID field. Refused at construction, because no octet string can represent it.

reject.name: sequence-count-above-fourteen-bit-field
reject.note: 16384 does not fit the 14-bit sequence count; one more would overflow into the sequence flags.

reject.name: empty-data-field
reject.note: The length field carries the data field size minus one, so a zero-octet data field has no representation: it would need a length field of -1. A packet must carry at least one octet after the header.
